intro: Some conversations make everyone nervous: telling a client their project will be late, speaking for your company when something has gone wrong, or telling a senior director that their plan has a risk. Today you'll learn a clear structure for each, so you can be honest and kind at the same time. Warm-up: think of the last time someone gave you bad news. What did they do well, and what made it worse?
teachingNotes: This functional lesson builds on c1-negotiation (the diplomatic no: I'm afraid that wouldn't work for us, because … + an alternative; summarising terms; next steps in writing), c1-leading-meetings (action points = who + what + by when; by Thursday = paling lambat; sungkan and musyawarah in meetings; Let's take that offline) and c2-implied-meaning (the polite code: I'm not sure that's the best idea = I disagree; soften + reason + alternative; be direct about safety, money and deadlines). Recap those in a line; don't re-teach them. New here: (1) delivering bad news with a structure, empathy and responsibility; (2) crisis communication: updates and holding statements; (3) disagreeing upward or with a client: acknowledge, evidence, alternative, leave the decision, and when to escalate. Contexts: a construction project for a client in Bandung or Cikarang, an IT outage at a bank in Jakarta, a food-safety problem at a restaurant chain in Surabaya, a data rumour at an online shop, a senior Pak/Bu director with a risky plan.

Bad news (deliver-bad-news). Be clear early: don't bury the news under background, and don't shrink it. The node's common error: 'Maybe there is a little problem with the deadline, but it's okay.' → 'I'm afraid we won't meet the 15 March deadline. Here's what we can do instead.' (the vague version sounds like no problem, so the client keeps planning around the old date; it often comes from translating 'ada sedikit kendala'). Structure: signal (one short line: I'm afraid I have some difficult news) → the news in one sentence → reason (brief, no excuses) → impact → what you're doing / options → next step (who + what + by when). Empathy without false comfort: I know this isn't what you were hoping for; I can imagine how frustrating this is; not 'Don't worry, it's nothing' or 'It'll all be fine' when you don't know that. Take responsibility with we: We made a mistake / that's on us, not 'Mistakes were made' or 'An error occurred' (like 'telah terjadi kesalahan', it hides who). One sincere apology, then action: five sorries sound like panic and shift the focus to your feelings. No blame: 'It's not our fault, the supplier …' → 'Our supplier delivered late, and we should have had a backup.' Accept 'I'm sorry, but …' / 'Unfortunately, …' as openings too; what matters is that the news comes early and clearly.

Crisis communication (crisis-communication). Every update answers four questions: what happened (facts only: what we know AND what we don't know yet), what we're doing, what people should do, when the next update comes (a time, not 'soon'). Short sentences, no speculation about causes ('It was probably a hacker' → 'We don't yet know the cause'), no promises you can't keep ('100% safe'), one spokesperson (juru bicara) so the messages don't contradict each other. Holding statement when you know almost nothing: We're aware of reports of … and are investigating. We'll update you by 3 p.m. Traps: 'No comment' sounds like hiding; 'We apologise for any inconvenience' (from 'mohon maaf atas ketidaknyamanannya') sounds cold when people lost money or got sick: say what happened and 'We're sorry. This should not have happened.' British apologise / American apologize.

Disagreeing upward or with a client (disagree-diplomatically). Four moves: acknowledge their goal (I can see why you want to …), state the concern with evidence (My concern is that … last year …), propose an alternative (Could we consider …?), leave the decision with them (It's your call, but I'd recommend … / Ultimately it's your decision). Raise it privately first when you can (Could I have five minutes after the meeting?). Name sungkan (feeling too uncomfortable to contradict someone senior) and 'asal bapak senang' (ABS: telling the boss only what pleases him) respectfully: respect for seniors is a real strength, but 'Yes, Pak' or silence is heard as full agreement, and a risky plan goes ahead. 'It's your call, but I'd recommend …' is not 'terserah': it keeps your recommendation. Exception: when safety, the law or ethics are at stake, drop the soft code and be direct: I can't sign this off: the scaffolding failed its inspection. / I'm not able to change the date on this document. Escalate if needed (I'll need to raise this with the safety team).

Limits and grading: at C2 every structure is available; the point is control and choice, not new forms. Much of this is style: accept reasonable alternatives (I'm afraid / Unfortunately / I'm sorry to tell you; My concern / My worry; It's your call / your decision / your choice) and only mark clear cases wrong: the news buried or shrunk, false comfort, a passive that hides responsibility, blame, speculation in a crisis, a blunt or a fake-agreeing reply to a senior person, or the soft code where safety or ethics demand directness. Don't teach crisis PR strategy, legal liability or media training beyond these moves. The app's audio is one calm voice: listen items depend on the words only. When the learner practises, play the client, the journalist or the director, react realistically (disappointed, impatient), then correct ONE thing, usually the buried news, 'Mistakes were made', a guessed cause, or 'Yes, Pak' instead of a concern.

keyPoints.title: Deliver bad news clearly, early and with empathy
keyPoints.explanation: Give the news in one clear sentence near the start: don't bury it under background and don't shrink it (Maybe there's a little problem, but it's okay sounds like no problem). Then: a brief reason (no excuses) → the impact → what you're doing or the options → the next step. Show empathy without false comfort (I know this isn't what you were hoping for), take responsibility with we (We made a mistake, not Mistakes were made), apologise once and sincerely, and don't blame others.

examples.en: I'm afraid we won't meet the 15 March deadline. Here's what we can do instead.
examples.id: Mohon maaf, kami tidak akan bisa memenuhi tenggat 15 Maret. Ini yang bisa kami lakukan sebagai gantinya.

examples.en: I know this isn't what you were hoping for.
examples.id: Saya tahu ini bukan yang Anda harapkan.

examples.en: We made a mistake with the load calculations, and that's on us.
examples.id: Kami salah menghitung beban, dan itu tanggung jawab kami.

id.title: Sampaikan kabar buruk dengan jelas, cepat dan empatik
id.explanation: Sampaikan kabarnya dalam satu kalimat jelas di awal: jangan menguburnya di bawah latar belakang panjang, dan jangan mengecilkannya (Maybe there's a little problem, but it's okay terdengar seperti tidak ada masalah). Lalu: alasan singkat (tanpa dalih) → dampaknya → apa yang sedang kamu lakukan atau pilihan-pilihannya → langkah berikutnya. Tunjukkan empati tanpa penghiburan palsu (I know this isn't what you were hoping for), ambil tanggung jawab dengan we (We made a mistake, bukan Mistakes were made), minta maaf sekali dengan tulus, dan jangan menyalahkan orang lain.

keyPoints.title: Communicate in a crisis: four questions
keyPoints.explanation: Every crisis update answers four questions: what happened (facts only: what you know and what you don't know yet), what you're doing, what people should do, and when the next update comes (a time, not 'soon'). Use short sentences, don't guess the cause, don't promise what you can't know, and let one spokesperson speak. If you know almost nothing yet, give a holding statement: We're aware of reports of … and are investigating. We'll update you by 3 p.m.

examples.en: Since 8 a.m., customers haven't been able to log in to our mobile app.
examples.id: Sejak pukul 08.00, nasabah tidak bisa masuk ke aplikasi seluler kami.

examples.en: We don't yet know the cause.
We're aware of reports of a fire at our Cikarang warehouse and are investigating. We'll update you by 3 p.m.
examples.id: Kami mengetahui adanya laporan kebakaran di gudang kami di Cikarang dan sedang menyelidikinya. Kami akan memberi kabar terbaru paling lambat pukul 15.00.

id.title: Berkomunikasi saat krisis: empat pertanyaan
id.explanation: Setiap kabar terbaru saat krisis menjawab empat pertanyaan: apa yang terjadi (fakta saja: apa yang sudah kamu ketahui dan apa yang belum), apa yang sedang kamu lakukan, apa yang perlu dilakukan orang, dan kapan kabar berikutnya (sebutkan jamnya, bukan 'secepatnya'). Pakai kalimat pendek, jangan menebak penyebabnya, jangan menjanjikan hal yang belum bisa kamu ketahui, dan biarkan satu juru bicara yang berbicara. Kalau kamu hampir belum tahu apa-apa, sampaikan holding statement (pernyataan sementara): We're aware of reports of … and are investigating. We'll update you by 3 p.m.

keyPoints.title: Disagree diplomatically with a manager or client
keyPoints.explanation: Four moves: acknowledge their goal (I can see why you want to …), state your concern with evidence (My concern is that … last year …), propose an alternative (Could we consider …?) and leave the decision with them (It's your call, but I'd recommend …). Raise it privately first if you can. Respect for seniors is a strength, but sungkan and 'asal bapak senang' turn it into silence, and in English 'Yes, Pak' sounds like full agreement. When safety, the law or ethics are at stake, be direct.

examples.en: I can see why you want a national launch, Bu Ratna. My concern is the budget: last year's campaign used 80% of it in the first month.
examples.id: Saya paham kenapa Ibu ingin peluncuran nasional, Bu Ratna. Yang saya khawatirkan anggarannya: kampanye tahun lalu memakai 80% anggaran di bulan pertama.

examples.en: Could we consider a pilot in three cities first? It's your call, but that's what I'd recommend.
examples.id: Bagaimana kalau kita pertimbangkan uji coba di tiga kota dulu? Keputusannya di tangan Ibu, tapi itu saran saya.

examples.en: Pak, I can't sign this off. The scaffolding failed its inspection, and someone could get hurt.
examples.id: Pak, saya tidak bisa menyetujui ini. Perancahnya tidak lolos inspeksi, dan bisa ada yang celaka.

id.title: Tidak setuju secara diplomatis dengan atasan atau klien
id.explanation: Empat langkah: akui tujuan mereka (I can see why you want to …), sampaikan kekhawatiranmu dengan bukti (My concern is that … last year …), usulkan alternatif (Could we consider …?) dan serahkan keputusannya kepada mereka (It's your call, but I'd recommend …). Kalau bisa, sampaikan empat mata dulu. Menghormati atasan itu kekuatan, tapi rasa sungkan dan budaya 'asal bapak senang' mengubahnya menjadi diam, dan dalam bahasa Inggris 'Yes, Pak' terdengar seperti setuju sepenuhnya. Kalau menyangkut keselamatan, hukum atau etika, bicaralah langsung.

guidedPractice.prompt: Budi's furniture workshop in Jepara can only deliver 40 of the 100 chairs a hotel in Bali ordered before its opening. He starts his call with: 'Maybe there's a small issue with the chairs, but it's okay.' Is that a good opening? Answer yes or no.
guidedPractice.hint: It shrinks the news: 'a small issue … but it's okay' sounds like no problem. Say the news itself, early: I'm afraid we can only deliver 40 of the chairs before the opening.

guidedPractice.prompt: Which of these two sentences hides who is responsible: 'We made a mistake with your order' or 'Mistakes were made with your order'? Write the sentence.
expected: mistakes were made with your order
guidedPractice.hint: A passive with no 'by …' doesn't say who did it. Indonesian 'telah terjadi kesalahan' does the same.

guidedPractice.prompt: The payment app of a startup in Jakarta has been down for an hour. The cause isn't known yet. The spokesperson wants to say: 'It was probably a cyber attack.' Should she say it? Answer yes or no.
guidedPractice.hint: In a crisis, say only what you know. If the cause isn't known yet, say so: We don't yet know the cause.

guidedPractice.prompt: A hospital in Bandung has a power cut, and the backup generator is working. Complete the last line of the update with one word: We'll ___ you another update at 4 p.m.
guidedPractice.hint: give someone an update = memberi kabar terbaru. Always end with a time for the next update.

guidedPractice.prompt: Your manager, Bu Ani, wants to move the office party to a Friday night. You think fewer people will come. Start by acknowledging her goal. Complete with one word: I can ___ why you want to make it more relaxed, Bu Ani.
guidedPractice.hint: I can see why … = saya paham kenapa …: the first move is to show you understand their goal.

independentPractice.prompt: You organise events in Bali. The villa your client booked for a team retreat on 12 August is no longer available because of a flood. Write the first sentence of your call: the news, clearly, starting with 'I'm afraid'.
expected: i'm afraid the villa won't be available on 12 august
i'm afraid the villa is no longer available on 12 august
i'm afraid the villa isn't available on 12 august
i am afraid the villa will not be available on 12 august
i'm afraid the villa you booked is no longer available
i'm afraid we've lost the villa for 12 august
i'm afraid the villa won't be available for your retreat
independentPractice.hint: One clear sentence with the news itself (the villa isn't available on 12 August). The reason (the flood) and the options come next.

independentPractice.prompt: Your director, Pak Hasan, wants to cut the staff training budget by half. You think the new software project needs the training. Write one sentence that states your concern with a piece of evidence, starting 'My concern is that…'.
expected: my concern is that the team hasn't used the new software before
my concern is that without training the new software project could be delayed
my concern is that last year's project was late because the team wasn't trained
my concern is that the new system needs trained staff
my concern is that we'll make more mistakes without the training
independentPractice.hint: Concern + evidence: a fact, a number or what happened last time, not just 'I don't like it'.

assessment.prompt: You manage a construction project for a client, PT Sinar Logistik. Their new warehouse in Cikarang won't be ready on 30 June: it will be about six weeks late. You call the client's director, and you want your first sentence to give the bad news clearly and politely, without hiding it. Complete with one word: I'm ___ we won't be able to hand over the warehouse by 30 June.
assessment.rubric: Correct: afraid (I'm afraid … = a polite, clear signal that bad news follows, and here the news itself comes straight after). 'sorry' = 100 (I'm sorry we won't be able to … is also natural and clear). 'sure' / 'certain' / 'thinking' / 'worried' = 30 (grammatical, but they make the news sound uncertain or about your feelings: the date is already lost). Any other word = 0.

assessment.prompt: Your team at an accounting firm in Bandung sent a client the wrong tax figures, and the client has noticed. On the call, you want to take responsibility clearly, instead of saying 'Mistakes were made.' Complete with one word: We ___ a mistake with your tax figures, and I'm sorry. We'll send you the corrected report by Thursday.
assessment.rubric: Correct: made (We made a mistake = we take responsibility; make a mistake is the fixed collocation). 'found' / 'noticed' / 'discovered' = 20 (grammatical and true, but it doesn't say who made the mistake: the responsibility disappears, like 'Mistakes were made'). 'did' = 30 (a common learner error: do a mistake is not natural English). Any other word = 0.

assessment.prompt: Posts on social media say that several customers became ill after eating at a restaurant chain's branch in Surabaya. The company doesn't know the facts yet, but it must say something within the hour. Complete the holding statement with one word: We're ___ of reports that several customers became ill after eating at our Tunjungan branch, and we're investigating. We'll share an update by 5 p.m.
assessment.rubric: Correct: aware (We're aware of reports … = we know people are saying this, without confirming or denying the facts yet; the standard opening of a holding statement). 'conscious' = 50 (grammatical, but it's not the usual phrase here). 'sure' / 'certain' = 0 (We're sure of reports … isn't natural, and it sounds as if the facts are confirmed). Any other word = 0.

assessment.prompt: Read this update from a bank in Jakarta: 'Since 9 a.m. today, some customers have been unable to use our mobile app. Card payments and ATMs are working normally. Our engineers are working to restore the service. In the meantime, please use any of our ATMs or call our 24-hour helpline.' A good crisis update answers four questions: what happened, what we're doing, what you should do, and when the next update comes. Which one is missing? Write it.
acceptableAnswers: when the next update will be
when the next update comes is missing
the time of the next update
when the next update will come
assessment.rubric: Correct: when the next update comes (what happened = the app is down since 9 a.m.; what we're doing = engineers restoring it; what you should do = use ATMs or call; there's no time for the next update). 'next update' / 'when' = 100. The idea in Indonesian (kapan kabar berikutnya) = 60. 'what happened' / 'what we're doing' / 'what you should do' = 0 (all three are in the text).

assessment.prompt: Your director, Pak Bambang, wants to open three new branches of your café chain in Medan at the same time next year. You think it's too risky. You ask to speak to him after the meeting. Complete with one word: I can see why you want to grow quickly, Pak. My ___ is that when we opened two branches at once in 2023, both lost money for the whole first year.
assessment.rubric: Correct: concern (My concern is that … = a calm, professional way to name a risk, followed here by evidence: what happened in 2023). 'worry' / 'fear' = 100. 'problem' = 50 (grammatical, but 'My problem is …' sounds personal and more confrontational). 'idea' / 'opinion' = 40 (they don't signal a risk). Any other word = 0.

assessment.prompt: Your client, Bu Ratna, wants her company's new app to launch on 1 December. You'd recommend 15 January, after the testing is finished. You've explained your reasons with evidence. Now you leave the final decision with her but keep your recommendation. Complete with one word: It's your ___, Bu Ratna, but I'd recommend waiting until the testing is finished.
assessment.rubric: Correct: call (It's your call = it's your decision: you leave the decision with her, and 'but I'd recommend …' keeps your view). 'decision' / 'choice' = 100. 'problem' / 'risk' = 0 (they blame the client instead of leaving the decision with her). Any other word = 0.

assessment.prompt: Your director, Pak Rudi, asks you to change the date on a document so that your company can still enter a government tender that closed yesterday. Should you answer with the soft polite code ('I'm not sure that's the best idea…') or say clearly and respectfully that you can't do it? Write one word: soft or direct.
assessment.rubric: Correct: direct (changing the date on a tender document is an ethical and legal problem; when ethics, the law or safety are at stake, the soft code can be heard as 'maybe', so say clearly and respectfully that you can't do it, and escalate if needed). The idea in Indonesian (langsung, tegas) = 60. 'soft' = 0.

material.title: Bad news: say it early, say it clearly

id.title: Kabar buruk: sampaikan di awal, sampaikan dengan jelas

blocks.text:
Quick recap: in the negotiation lesson you said no with *I'm afraid that wouldn't work for us, because …* + an alternative; when chairing meetings you gave action points with **who + what + by when**; and in the implied-meaning lesson you learnt the polite code. Now the hardest version: news that nobody wants to hear.

**The two big mistakes** are **burying** the news (ten minutes of background before you get to it) and **shrinking** it (*a little problem, but it's okay*). Both leave the listener unsure what happened, and the longer they wait, the worse it feels.

**A structure that works:**
- **Signal**: one short line, so they're ready: *I'm afraid I have some difficult news.*
- **The news, in one sentence**, near the start: *We won't meet the 15 March deadline.*
- **Reason**: brief, no excuses: *The steel arrived six weeks late.*
- **Impact**: what it means for them: *You won't be able to move in before April.*
- **What you're doing / the options**: *Here's what we can do instead: …*
- **Next step**: who + what + by when: *I'll send you a revised schedule by Friday.*

id.text:
Ulang singkat: di pelajaran negosiasi kamu menolak dengan *I'm afraid that wouldn't work for us, because …* + alternatif; saat memimpin rapat kamu memberi poin tindak lanjut dengan **siapa + apa + paling lambat kapan**; dan di pelajaran makna tersirat kamu belajar kode sopan. Sekarang versi paling sulit: kabar yang tidak ingin didengar siapa pun.

**Dua kesalahan besar** adalah **mengubur** kabarnya (sepuluh menit latar belakang sebelum sampai ke intinya) dan **mengecilkannya** (*a little problem, but it's okay*). Keduanya membuat pendengar tidak yakin apa yang sebenarnya terjadi, dan makin lama mereka menunggu, makin buruk rasanya.

**Struktur yang berhasil:**
- **Sinyal**: satu kalimat pendek, supaya mereka siap: *I'm afraid I have some difficult news.*
- **Kabarnya, dalam satu kalimat**, di awal: *We won't meet the 15 March deadline.*
- **Alasan**: singkat, tanpa dalih: *The steel arrived six weeks late.*
- **Dampak**: artinya bagi mereka: *You won't be able to move in before April.*
- **Apa yang sedang kamu lakukan / pilihannya**: *Here's what we can do instead: …*
- **Langkah berikutnya**: siapa + apa + paling lambat kapan: *I'll send you a revised schedule by Friday.*

rows.en: I'm afraid I have some difficult news about the Bandung office project.
rows.id: Mohon maaf, ada kabar kurang baik tentang proyek kantor di Bandung.

rows.en: We won't meet the 15 March deadline: we now expect to finish on 26 April.
rows.id: Kami tidak akan bisa memenuhi tenggat 15 Maret: sekarang kami perkirakan selesai 26 April.

rows.en: The steel arrived six weeks late, and we didn't have a backup supplier.
rows.id: Bajanya datang terlambat enam minggu, dan kami tidak punya pemasok cadangan.
rows.note: reason: brief, and it owns our part

id.note: alasan: singkat, dan mengakui bagian kami

rows.en: That means your team can't move in before your current lease ends.
rows.id: Artinya tim Anda belum bisa pindah sebelum masa sewa kantor sekarang habis.

rows.en: We've added a second shift, and we can rent you temporary space nearby at our cost.
rows.id: Kami sudah menambah satu shift, dan kami bisa menyewakan ruang sementara di dekat sana atas biaya kami.

rows.en: I'll send you a revised schedule by Friday.
rows.id: Saya akan mengirim jadwal yang sudah direvisi paling lambat Jumat.
rows.note: next step: who + what + by when

id.note: langkah berikutnya: siapa + apa + paling lambat kapan

blocks.text:
**The commonest mistake:** `Maybe there is a little problem with the deadline, but it's okay.` ✗ It often comes from *ada sedikit kendala*, which in Indonesian can politely cover a big problem. In English it sounds like **no** problem, so the client keeps planning around the old date and feels misled later. Say: **I'm afraid we won't meet the 15 March deadline. Here's what we can do instead.**

**Short signal, then the news.** One line of warning is kind (*I'm afraid I have some difficult news*); a long build-up is not. *I'm sorry, but …* and *Unfortunately, …* work too.

id.text:
**Kesalahan paling umum:** `Maybe there is a little problem with the deadline, but it's okay.` ✗ Ini sering berasal dari *ada sedikit kendala*, yang dalam bahasa Indonesia bisa dengan sopan menutupi masalah besar. Dalam bahasa Inggris, kalimat itu terdengar seperti **tidak ada** masalah, jadi klien tetap merencanakan dengan tanggal lama dan merasa dibohongi belakangan. Katakan: **I'm afraid we won't meet the 15 March deadline. Here's what we can do instead.**

**Sinyal singkat, lalu kabarnya.** Satu kalimat peringatan itu baik (*I'm afraid I have some difficult news*); basa-basi panjang tidak. *I'm sorry, but …* dan *Unfortunately, …* juga bisa.

blocks.prompt: A printing company in Yogyakarta can only print 2,000 of the 5,000 brochures a client ordered before her conference on Saturday. The other 3,000 can be ready on Monday. Which is the best opening for the call?
options: As you know, paper prices have gone up this year, and two of our staff are ill, and the machine is quite old, so…
I'm afraid we can only print 2,000 brochures before Saturday. The other 3,000 will be ready on Monday.
There's a little problem with the printer, but it's okay, don't worry.
blocks.explain: The second option gives the news in the first sentence and is clear about the numbers and dates. The first buries the news under excuses (and the client still doesn't know what's happening). The third shrinks it: 'a little problem … it's okay' sounds like everything will arrive on time.

id.prompt: Sebuah percetakan di Yogyakarta hanya bisa mencetak 2.000 dari 5.000 brosur yang dipesan klien sebelum konferensinya hari Sabtu. Sisanya, 3.000, bisa siap hari Senin. Mana pembuka telepon yang paling tepat?
id.explain: Pilihan kedua menyampaikan kabarnya di kalimat pertama dan jelas soal jumlah dan tanggalnya. Pilihan pertama mengubur kabarnya di bawah dalih (dan klien tetap belum tahu apa yang terjadi). Pilihan ketiga mengecilkannya: 'a little problem … it's okay' terdengar seperti semuanya akan datang tepat waktu.

material.title: Empathy, responsibility and one good apology

id.title: Empati, tanggung jawab, dan satu permintaan maaf yang tulus

blocks.text:
Clear doesn't mean cold. Three habits make bad news easier to hear and keep the relationship:
- **Empathy without false comfort.** Show you understand what it means for them: ***I know this isn't what you were hoping for.*** / ***I can imagine how frustrating this is.*** But don't promise what you don't know: `Don't worry, it'll all be fine` ✗ sounds kind today and dishonest next week.
- **Take responsibility with *we*.** ***We made a mistake with the load calculations, and that's on us.*** (*that's on us* = itu tanggung jawab kami). A passive with no *by …* hides who did it: `Mistakes were made` ✗ / `An error occurred` ✗, just like *telah terjadi kesalahan*.
- **One sincere apology, then action.** ***I'm sorry. Here's how we're going to put it right.*** (*put it right* = memperbaikinya). Five sorries in a row sound like panic and turn the conversation to your feelings instead of their problem.

id.text:
Jelas bukan berarti dingin. Tiga kebiasaan ini membuat kabar buruk lebih mudah diterima dan menjaga hubungan:
- **Empati tanpa penghiburan palsu.** Tunjukkan kamu paham artinya bagi mereka: ***I know this isn't what you were hoping for.*** / ***I can imagine how frustrating this is.*** Tapi jangan menjanjikan hal yang kamu sendiri belum tahu: `Don't worry, it'll all be fine` ✗ terdengar baik hari ini dan terdengar tidak jujur minggu depan.
- **Ambil tanggung jawab dengan *we*.** ***We made a mistake with the load calculations, and that's on us.*** (*that's on us* = itu tanggung jawab kami). Kalimat pasif tanpa *by …* menyembunyikan siapa pelakunya: `Mistakes were made` ✗ / `An error occurred` ✗, persis seperti *telah terjadi kesalahan*.
- **Satu permintaan maaf yang tulus, lalu tindakan.** ***I'm sorry. Here's how we're going to put it right.*** (*put it right* = memperbaikinya). Lima kali minta maaf berturut-turut terdengar panik dan membuat percakapan berpusat pada perasaanmu, bukan masalah mereka.

rows.en: I know this isn't what you were hoping for.
rows.id: Saya tahu ini bukan yang Anda harapkan.

rows.en: I can imagine how frustrating this is, especially before your opening.
rows.id: Saya bisa membayangkan betapa menjengkelkannya ini, apalagi menjelang pembukaan Anda.

rows.en: We made a mistake with the load calculations, and that's on us.
rows.id: Kami salah menghitung beban, dan itu tanggung jawab kami.

rows.en: Our supplier delivered late, and we should have had a backup.
rows.id: Pemasok kami terlambat mengirim, dan seharusnya kami punya cadangan.

rows.en: I'm sorry. Here's how we're going to put it right.
rows.id: Saya minta maaf. Begini cara kami akan memperbaikinya.

blocks.text:
**Four habits to avoid:**
- **False comfort:** `It's nothing, don't worry` ✗ when it's something.
- **Hiding behind a passive:** `Mistakes were made` ✗ → *We made a mistake.*
- **Over-apologising:** `We're so, so sorry, we're terribly sorry, please forgive us…` ✗ → one *I'm sorry*, then the plan.
- **Blame:** `It's not our fault, the supplier messed up` ✗ → *Our supplier delivered late, and we should have had a backup.* The client chose you, not your supplier.

**British vs American:** *apologise* (British) / *apologize* (American).

id.text:
**Empat kebiasaan yang perlu dihindari:**
- **Penghiburan palsu:** `It's nothing, don't worry` ✗ padahal masalahnya nyata.
- **Bersembunyi di balik kalimat pasif:** `Mistakes were made` ✗ → *We made a mistake.*
- **Terlalu banyak minta maaf:** `We're so, so sorry, we're terribly sorry, please forgive us…` ✗ → satu *I'm sorry*, lalu rencananya.
- **Menyalahkan:** `It's not our fault, the supplier messed up` ✗ → *Our supplier delivered late, and we should have had a backup.* Klien memilih kamu, bukan pemasokmu.

**British vs Amerika:** *apologise* (British) / *apologize* (Amerika).

blocks.prompt: A catering company in Yogyakarta brought 50 portions too few to a client's company dinner. Which reply to the client takes responsibility, without blame or over-apologising?
options: Mistakes were made in the kitchen, and our new staff are to blame.
We're so sorry, we're terribly, terribly sorry, we feel awful, we're so sorry.
We got the numbers wrong, and I'm sorry. We'll refund the 50 portions and give you a discount on your next order.
blocks.explain: The third reply owns the mistake with 'we', apologises once and moves to action. The first hides behind a passive (Mistakes were made) and then blames the staff. The second only apologises: there's no plan, and the client ends up comforting you.

id.prompt: Sebuah perusahaan katering di Yogyakarta membawa 50 porsi kurang di acara makan malam kantor seorang klien. Jawaban mana untuk klien yang mengambil tanggung jawab, tanpa menyalahkan dan tanpa minta maaf berlebihan?
id.explain: Jawaban ketiga mengakui kesalahan dengan 'we', minta maaf sekali, lalu langsung ke tindakan. Jawaban pertama bersembunyi di balik kalimat pasif (Mistakes were made) lalu menyalahkan staf. Jawaban kedua hanya minta maaf: tidak ada rencana, dan kliennya malah harus menghibur kamu.

material.title: Crisis communication: four questions, short sentences

id.title: Komunikasi krisis: empat pertanyaan, kalimat pendek

blocks.text:
A crisis is bad news in public, fast, with only half the facts. People are worried, and every word may be quoted. Every update answers **four questions**:
- **What happened?** Facts only. Say what you know **and what you don't know yet**: *We don't yet know the cause.*
- **What are we doing?** *Our engineers are working to restore the service.*
- **What should people do?** *In the meantime, please use our ATMs.*
- **When is the next update?** A time, not *soon*: *We'll give you our next update at 11 a.m.*

**Short sentences.** One fact per sentence, so nobody can misread or cut a quote.
**No speculation** (menebak-nebak): `It was probably a hacker` ✗ may be wrong, and then nobody trusts the next update.
**One spokesperson** (juru bicara): if three managers give three versions, the story becomes the confusion.

**Holding statement** (pernyataan sementara): when you know almost nothing yet, still say something, quickly: ***We're aware of reports of a fire at our Cikarang warehouse and are investigating. We'll update you by 3 p.m.***

id.text:
Krisis adalah kabar buruk di depan publik, serba cepat, dengan fakta yang baru setengah. Orang khawatir, dan setiap kata bisa dikutip. Setiap kabar terbaru menjawab **empat pertanyaan**:
- **Apa yang terjadi?** Fakta saja. Sebutkan apa yang sudah kamu ketahui **dan apa yang belum**: *We don't yet know the cause.*
- **Apa yang sedang kami lakukan?** *Our engineers are working to restore the service.*
- **Apa yang perlu dilakukan orang?** *In the meantime, please use our ATMs.*
- **Kapan kabar berikutnya?** Sebutkan jamnya, bukan *soon*: *We'll give you our next update at 11 a.m.*

**Kalimat pendek.** Satu fakta per kalimat, supaya tidak ada yang salah baca atau memotong kutipan.
**Jangan menebak-nebak:** `It was probably a hacker` ✗ bisa saja salah, dan setelah itu tidak ada yang percaya kabar berikutnya.
**Satu juru bicara:** kalau tiga manajer memberi tiga versi, yang jadi berita justru kebingungannya.

**Holding statement** (pernyataan sementara): saat kamu hampir belum tahu apa-apa, tetap sampaikan sesuatu, dengan cepat: ***We're aware of reports of a fire at our Cikarang warehouse and are investigating. We'll update you by 3 p.m.***

rows.en: Since 8 a.m. today, customers haven't been able to log in to our mobile app.
rows.id: Sejak pukul 08.00 hari ini, nasabah tidak bisa masuk ke aplikasi seluler kami.

rows.en: ATMs and card payments are working normally. We don't yet know the cause.
rows.id: ATM dan pembayaran kartu berjalan normal. Kami belum tahu penyebabnya.
rows.note: what we know, and what we don't

rows.en: Our engineers are working to restore the service.
rows.id: Teknisi kami sedang berupaya memulihkan layanan.

rows.en: In the meantime, please use our ATMs. Never share your PIN or OTP with anyone who calls you.
rows.id: Sementara itu, silakan gunakan ATM kami. Jangan pernah memberikan PIN atau OTP kepada siapa pun yang menelepon Anda.

rows.en: We'll give you our next update at 11 a.m.
rows.id: Kami akan memberi kabar terbaru berikutnya pukul 11.00.

blocks.text:
**Three traps:**
- **`No comment.` ✗** (*tidak ada komentar*) sounds like hiding something. Even with no facts, give a holding statement.
- **`We apologise for any inconvenience.` ✗** (from *mohon maaf atas ketidaknyamanannya*) is fine for a delayed train, but when people lost money or got sick, *inconvenience* sounds cold and makes the harm smaller. Say what happened and: ***We're sorry. This should not have happened.***
- **Promises you can't keep:** `Your data is 100% safe` ✗ before you know. Say what you've checked so far.

id.text:
**Tiga jebakan:**
- **`No comment.` ✗** (*tidak ada komentar*) terdengar seperti menyembunyikan sesuatu. Walaupun belum ada fakta, sampaikan holding statement.
- **`We apologise for any inconvenience.` ✗** (dari *mohon maaf atas ketidaknyamanannya*) wajar untuk kereta yang terlambat, tapi kalau orang kehilangan uang atau jatuh sakit, *inconvenience* terdengar dingin dan mengecilkan kerugiannya. Katakan apa yang terjadi, lalu: ***We're sorry. This should not have happened.***
- **Janji yang belum tentu bisa ditepati:** `Your data is 100% safe` ✗ sebelum kamu tahu. Sebutkan apa yang sudah kamu periksa sejauh ini.

blocks.prompt: A fire broke out at a factory in Cikarang this morning. It's now out. The spokesperson is preparing the first update. Which sentence should she NOT say yet?
options: The fire started at about 6 a.m. in the storage area.
It was probably caused by an electrical fault.
All 120 staff on the morning shift are safe.
blocks.explain: 'Probably caused by …' is speculation: the cause isn't known yet, and a wrong guess destroys trust. The time, the place and the staff count are facts, and saying them is exactly right. Instead: 'We don't yet know the cause. Fire investigators are on site.'

id.prompt: Pagi ini terjadi kebakaran di sebuah pabrik di Cikarang. Apinya sekarang sudah padam. Juru bicaranya sedang menyiapkan kabar pertama. Kalimat mana yang BELUM boleh ia ucapkan?
id.explain: 'Probably caused by …' adalah tebakan: penyebabnya belum diketahui, dan tebakan yang salah merusak kepercayaan. Jam, tempat dan jumlah staf adalah fakta, dan menyampaikannya sudah tepat. Sebagai gantinya: 'We don't yet know the cause. Fire investigators are on site.'

material.title: Disagreeing with a manager or a client

id.title: Tidak setuju dengan atasan atau klien

blocks.text:
In the implied-meaning lesson you learnt to disagree politely: **soften + reason + alternative**. With a manager or a client the stakes are higher: they decide, and the relationship matters. Use **four moves**:
1. **Acknowledge their goal**: show you understand *why* they want it. ***I can see why you want a national launch, Bu Ratna.***
2. **State your concern with evidence**: a fact, a number, what happened last time. ***My concern is the budget: last year's campaign used 80% of it in the first month.***
3. **Propose an alternative**: ***Could we consider a pilot in three cities first?***
4. **Leave the decision with them**, but keep your recommendation: ***It's your call, but that's what I'd recommend.*** / ***Ultimately it's your decision.*** (*It's your call* = keputusannya di tangan Anda.)

**Where:** raise it privately first if you can: ***Could I have five minutes after the meeting?*** A senior person can change their mind more easily without an audience.

**When to drop the soft code:** when **safety, the law or ethics** are at stake, *I'm not sure that's the best idea* can be heard as *maybe*. Be respectful but direct, and escalate if needed: ***Pak, I can't sign this off. The scaffolding failed its inspection, and someone could get hurt.***

id.text:
Di pelajaran makna tersirat kamu belajar tidak setuju dengan sopan: **lunakkan + alasan + alternatif**. Dengan atasan atau klien taruhannya lebih besar: merekalah yang memutuskan, dan hubungannya penting. Pakai **empat langkah**:
1. **Akui tujuan mereka**: tunjukkan kamu paham *kenapa* mereka menginginkannya. ***I can see why you want a national launch, Bu Ratna.***
2. **Sampaikan kekhawatiranmu dengan bukti**: fakta, angka, apa yang terjadi terakhir kali. ***My concern is the budget: last year's campaign used 80% of it in the first month.***
3. **Usulkan alternatif**: ***Could we consider a pilot in three cities first?***
4. **Serahkan keputusannya kepada mereka**, tapi tetap sampaikan saranmu: ***It's your call, but that's what I'd recommend.*** / ***Ultimately it's your decision.*** (*It's your call* = keputusannya di tangan Anda.)

**Di mana:** kalau bisa, sampaikan empat mata dulu: ***Could I have five minutes after the meeting?*** Atasan lebih mudah berubah pikiran tanpa penonton.

**Kapan berhenti memakai kode halus:** kalau menyangkut **keselamatan, hukum atau etika**, *I'm not sure that's the best idea* bisa terdengar seperti *mungkin*. Tetap hormat tapi langsung, dan eskalasikan kalau perlu: ***Pak, I can't sign this off. The scaffolding failed its inspection, and someone could get hurt.***

rows.en: I can see why you want to open before Lebaran, Pak.
rows.id: Saya paham kenapa Bapak ingin buka sebelum Lebaran.

rows.en: My concern is that the kitchen equipment won't arrive until the 20th.
rows.id: Yang saya khawatirkan, peralatan dapurnya baru datang tanggal 20.

rows.en: What if we opened the café first and the restaurant two weeks later?
rows.id: Bagaimana kalau kafenya buka dulu, dan restorannya dua minggu kemudian?

rows.en: Ultimately it's your decision, but I'd strongly recommend waiting.
rows.id: Pada akhirnya keputusannya di tangan Bapak, tapi saya sangat menyarankan untuk menunggu.
rows.note: leave the decision, keep the recommendation

rows.en: I'm not able to do that, Pak. It would break the tender rules. I'll need to check with the legal team.
rows.id: Saya tidak bisa melakukannya, Pak. Itu melanggar aturan tender. Saya perlu memeriksanya dengan tim legal.
rows.note: ethics or the law: direct, and escalate

id.note: etika atau hukum: langsung, dan eskalasikan

blocks.text:
**Sungkan and 'asal bapak senang'.** Respect for seniors (*hormat*) is a real strength of Indonesian workplaces, and you don't have to give it up. But *sungkan* (feeling too uncomfortable to contradict someone senior) and *asal bapak senang* (ABS: telling the boss only what pleases him) can let a risky plan go ahead while everyone sees the risk. In English, *Yes, Pak* or silence is heard as **full agreement**, and many managers, Indonesian and international, expect you to raise a concern. The four moves let you be respectful **and** honest.

**`Terserah Bapak` ≠ *It's your call, but I'd recommend …*** *Terserah* on its own can sound like giving up. *It's your call, **but I'd recommend …*** leaves the decision with them and still gives your view.

id.text:
**Sungkan dan 'asal bapak senang'.** Menghormati atasan adalah kekuatan nyata di tempat kerja Indonesia, dan kamu tidak perlu meninggalkannya. Tapi rasa *sungkan* dan budaya *asal bapak senang* (ABS: hanya menyampaikan yang menyenangkan atasan) bisa membuat rencana berisiko tetap jalan padahal semua orang melihat risikonya. Dalam bahasa Inggris, *Yes, Pak* atau diam didengar sebagai **setuju sepenuhnya**, dan banyak manajer, baik orang Indonesia maupun internasional, berharap kamu menyampaikan kekhawatiran. Empat langkah ini membuatmu bisa tetap hormat **dan** jujur.

**`Terserah Bapak` ≠ *It's your call, but I'd recommend …*** *Terserah* saja bisa terdengar seperti menyerah. *It's your call, **but I'd recommend …*** menyerahkan keputusan kepada mereka sambil tetap menyampaikan pendapatmu.

blocks.prompt: Your client, Bu Ratna, still prefers the national launch after hearing your evidence. You want to leave the decision with her but keep your recommendation. Which reply fits best?
options: You're wrong about this, Bu Ratna. We're doing the pilot.
Ultimately it's your decision, Bu Ratna, but I'd still recommend the pilot.
blocks.explain: The third reply leaves the decision with the client (Ultimately it's your decision) and keeps your view (but I'd still recommend …). 'Whatever you want' gives up your recommendation, like 'terserah'. 'You're wrong … We're doing the pilot' is far too blunt, and it isn't your decision to make.

id.prompt: Klienmu, Bu Ratna, tetap memilih peluncuran nasional setelah mendengar buktimu. Kamu ingin menyerahkan keputusan kepadanya tapi tetap menyampaikan saranmu. Jawaban mana yang paling pas?
id.explain: Jawaban ketiga menyerahkan keputusan kepada klien (Ultimately it's your decision) dan tetap menyampaikan pendapatmu (but I'd still recommend …). 'Whatever you want' melepaskan saranmu, seperti 'terserah'. 'You're wrong … We're doing the pilot' terlalu kasar, dan keputusannya bukan di tanganmu.

suggestedQuestions: How do I give bad news to a client without sounding cold or making excuses?
What should a holding statement say when we don't know the facts yet?
How can I disagree with a senior Pak or Bu director without being disrespectful?
When should I stop being indirect and just say no?

resources.title: How to Give Bad News: 6 Easy English Expressions
resources.note: A short, easy video with six expressions for giving bad news, for personal life as well as work. It's below this lesson's level and doesn't cover structure, crisis updates or disagreeing, but it's a relaxed way to hear the phrases in use.

id.note: Video singkat dan mudah berisi enam ungkapan untuk menyampaikan kabar buruk, untuk kehidupan pribadi maupun pekerjaan. Levelnya di bawah pelajaran ini dan tidak membahas struktur, kabar krisis atau cara tidak setuju, tapi cara santai untuk mendengar ungkapan-ungkapan itu dipakai.

resources.title: How to Give Bad News in English
resources.note: Seven steps for giving bad news (prepare, be direct, give time, give the facts, be caring, offer support, don't take it personally), with phrases for each and a video lesson. Close to this lesson's structure; a few of its 'caring' phrases are better avoided at work.

id.note: Tujuh langkah menyampaikan kabar buruk (bersiap, langsung ke inti, beri waktu, sampaikan faktanya, tunjukkan kepedulian, tawarkan dukungan, jangan dimasukkan ke hati), dengan ungkapan untuk setiap langkah dan sebuah video. Mirip dengan struktur pelajaran ini; beberapa ungkapan 'peduli'-nya sebaiknya tidak dipakai di tempat kerja.

resources.title: How to disagree politely in English
resources.note: The lesson page (video + quiz) on disagreeing politely with a boss, colleague or client, including body language and a four-step method (apologise, acknowledge, answer, ask). It suggests 'I hear you, and …' instead of 'but': a style choice, close to this lesson's 'acknowledge the goal' move.

id.note: Halaman pelajaran (video + kuis) tentang cara tidak setuju dengan sopan kepada atasan, rekan kerja atau klien, termasuk bahasa tubuh dan metode empat langkah (minta maaf, akui, jawab, tanya). Video ini menyarankan 'I hear you, and …' sebagai ganti 'but': pilihan gaya, mirip dengan langkah 'akui tujuannya' di pelajaran ini.

id.intro: Ada percakapan yang membuat siapa pun gugup: memberi tahu klien bahwa proyeknya akan terlambat, berbicara atas nama perusahaan saat terjadi masalah, atau menyampaikan kepada direktur senior bahwa rencananya berisiko. Hari ini kamu belajar struktur yang jelas untuk masing-masing, supaya kamu bisa jujur dan tetap baik sekaligus. Pemanasan: ingat terakhir kali seseorang menyampaikan kabar buruk kepadamu. Apa yang ia lakukan dengan baik, dan apa yang membuatnya makin buruk?
suggestedQuestions: Bagaimana menyampaikan kabar buruk ke klien tanpa terdengar dingin atau mencari-cari alasan?
Apa isi holding statement kalau kami belum tahu faktanya?
Bagaimana cara tidak setuju dengan direktur senior (Pak atau Bu) tanpa terkesan tidak hormat?
Kapan aku harus berhenti bicara tidak langsung dan langsung bilang tidak?

assessment.hs-1: Kamu mengelola proyek konstruksi untuk klien, PT Sinar Logistik. Gudang baru mereka di Cikarang tidak akan siap pada 30 Juni: terlambat sekitar enam minggu. Kamu menelepon direktur klien, dan kamu ingin kalimat pertamamu menyampaikan kabar buruknya dengan jelas dan sopan, tanpa menyembunyikannya. Lengkapi dengan satu kata: I'm ___ we won't be able to hand over the warehouse by 30 June.
assessment.hs-2: Tim kamu di sebuah kantor akuntan di Bandung mengirim angka pajak yang salah ke klien, dan kliennya sudah menyadarinya. Di telepon, kamu ingin mengambil tanggung jawab dengan jelas, bukan berkata 'Mistakes were made.' Lengkapi dengan satu kata: We ___ a mistake with your tax figures, and I'm sorry. We'll send you the corrected report by Thursday.
assessment.hs-3: Unggahan di media sosial menyebutkan beberapa pelanggan jatuh sakit setelah makan di salah satu cabang jaringan restoran di Surabaya. Perusahaannya belum tahu faktanya, tapi harus menyampaikan sesuatu dalam satu jam. Lengkapi holding statement-nya dengan satu kata: We're ___ of reports that several customers became ill after eating at our Tunjungan branch, and we're investigating. We'll share an update by 5 p.m.
assessment.hs-4: Baca kabar terbaru dari sebuah bank di Jakarta ini: 'Since 9 a.m. today, some customers have been unable to use our mobile app. Card payments and ATMs are working normally. Our engineers are working to restore the service. In the meantime, please use any of our ATMs or call our 24-hour helpline.' Kabar krisis yang baik menjawab empat pertanyaan: what happened, what we're doing, what you should do, dan when the next update comes. Mana yang tidak ada? Tulis dalam bahasa Inggris.
assessment.hs-5: Direkturmu, Pak Bambang, ingin membuka tiga cabang baru jaringan kafe kalian di Medan sekaligus tahun depan. Menurutmu itu terlalu berisiko. Kamu minta waktu bicara dengannya setelah rapat. Lengkapi dengan satu kata: I can see why you want to grow quickly, Pak. My ___ is that when we opened two branches at once in 2023, both lost money for the whole first year.
assessment.hs-6: Klienmu, Bu Ratna, ingin aplikasi baru perusahaannya diluncurkan 1 Desember. Kamu menyarankan 15 Januari, setelah pengujian selesai. Kamu sudah menjelaskan alasanmu dengan bukti. Sekarang kamu menyerahkan keputusan akhirnya kepadanya, tapi tetap menyampaikan saranmu. Lengkapi dengan satu kata: It's your ___, Bu Ratna, but I'd recommend waiting until the testing is finished.
assessment.hs-7: Direkturmu, Pak Rudi, memintamu mengubah tanggal di sebuah dokumen supaya perusahaanmu masih bisa ikut tender pemerintah yang sudah ditutup kemarin. Sebaiknya kamu menjawab dengan kode sopan yang halus ('I'm not sure that's the best idea…') atau mengatakan dengan jelas dan hormat bahwa kamu tidak bisa melakukannya? Tulis satu kata dalam bahasa Inggris: soft atau direct.
